about.name: Road trip packing list for India

intro: A road trip packing list has two parts: what the car needs, and what the people in it need. On India's roads, where help can be hours away in the mountains and delays are common in the monsoon, a well-stocked car kit is as important as your clothes.
Start with the core lists below, then add the extras for your route and season.
quickAnswer: For a road trip in India, pack your driving licence, car papers and FASTag; a car kit with a spare tyre, jack, tow rope, jump leads, torch and warning triangle; a first-aid kit and medicines; water, snacks and a cool box; phone chargers, a power bank and offline maps; and cash. Add warm layers and altitude medicines advised by a doctor for the mountains, and rain gear for the monsoon.
takeaways: Check the spare tyre, jack and wheel spanner before you leave.
Carry cash; network and card machines fail in remote areas.
Download offline maps for areas with weak signal.
Carry more water than you think you need.
Tailor extras to the route: mountains, monsoon, winter or family.

sections.heading: Documents and money
list: Driving licence and ID for all adults.
Registration certificate, insurance and pollution certificate (originals or DigiLocker copies).
Rental agreement, if applicable.
FASTag with enough balance.
Permits for Ladakh, Arunachal, Sikkim or Rohtang, printed and on your phone.
Cash in small notes, plus cards and UPI.

sections.heading: Car emergency kit
list: Inflated spare tyre, jack and wheel spanner.
Puncture repair kit or tyre inflator.
Tow rope and jump leads.
Torch with spare batteries.
Warning triangle and a reflective vest.
Basic tools, spare fuses and a bottle of coolant.
Microfibre cloths and a windscreen cleaner.
A small fire extinguisher, if your car has space for one.

sections.heading: First aid, food and comfort
list: First-aid kit with bandages, antiseptic, pain relief and personal medicines.
Motion-sickness tablets, oral rehydration salts and stomach medicines.
Plenty of drinking water, snacks and a cool box.
Tissues, wet wipes, hand sanitiser and waste bags.
Sunglasses, sunscreen and a hat.
A light blanket and neck pillow.

sections.heading: Electronics and navigation
list: Phone mount and car charger.
Power bank.
Offline maps and saved stay contacts.
Downloaded music, podcasts or audiobooks for areas without signal.

sections.heading: Extras for mountain and high-altitude drives
list: Warm layers, a windproof jacket, gloves and a woollen cap, even in summer.
Medicines for altitude sickness only as advised by a doctor.
Lip balm and strong sunscreen.
Snow chains or local advice in winter.
Extra food and water for long gaps between stops.

sections.heading: Extras for the monsoon
list: Rain jackets and umbrellas for everyone.
Spare dry clothes in a waterproof bag.
Anti-fog cloth or spray for windows.
Newspaper or mats for wet shoes.

sections.heading: Extras for winter and snow
list: Thermals and a warm jacket.
A thermos for hot drinks.
De-icer or a scraper for early mornings in the hills.
Snow chains where they may be required.

sections.heading: Extras for family road trips
list: Child car seat.
Games, books and downloaded entertainment.
Sick bags and a change of clothes for children.
Favourite snacks and a small treat for each day.

sections.heading: For motorcycle trips
paras: Riders need a certified helmet, riding jacket, gloves, boots and rain gear, plus a tool kit, spare tubes or a puncture kit, and luggage straps. Our Adventure guides cover riding kit in more detail.

safety: Keep heavy luggage in the boot or tied down; loose items can injure passengers in a sudden stop.
Mountain roads close or slow down after heavy rain, snow or landslides; check road status and weather updates each morning and avoid driving after dark.
Permits, tolls, entry fees, pass openings and road works change; check official sources shortly before you travel.
Distances and driving times are approximate and vary with traffic, weather, road works and stops.
packing: Driving licence, RC, insurance and PUC certificate, with copies
Warm layers and a rain jacket
Cash for small towns and barriers

faqs.q: What should I pack for a road trip in India?
faqs.a: Documents and FASTag, a car emergency kit, first aid, water and snacks, chargers and offline maps, and cash.

faqs.q: What car essentials should I carry?
faqs.a: A spare tyre, jack, wheel spanner, tow rope, jump leads, torch and warning triangle.

faqs.q: What should I pack for a mountain road trip?
faqs.a: Warm layers even in summer, sunscreen, and altitude medicines only as advised by a doctor.

faqs.q: What should I pack for a monsoon road trip?
faqs.a: Rain jackets, umbrellas, dry clothes in a waterproof bag and anti-fog cloths.

faqs.q: What should I pack for a family road trip?
faqs.a: A child seat, entertainment, snacks, sick bags and spare clothes for children.

faqs.q: Do I need cash on a road trip in India?
faqs.a: Yes; card machines and UPI can fail where the network is weak.
